Class EquinixClient

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.core.client.EquinixClient
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public class EquinixClient extends Object implements Closeable
Low-level transport client: owns the OAuth2 token lifecycle, the pooled HTTP client, the resolved endpoint, and the merged apiParams catalogue, and signs and dispatches every request. The public facade EquinixClient and the domain clients delegate to an instance of this class.
Author:
ianjones

      public EquinixClient(EquinixCredentials equinixCredentials, boolean isSandBoxed)

    • EquinixClient

      public EquinixClient(EquinixCredentialsProvider credentialsProvider, boolean isSandBoxed)
      Creates a transport client that resolves its credentials through the given provider. The provider is consulted on each authentication (first call and re-auth on expiry), so a custom provider can rotate the underlying credentials without the client being rebuilt.
      Parameters:
      credentialsProvider - supplies the OAuth2 credentials to authenticate with
      isSandBoxed - true for the sandbox environment; false for production

      public void setCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreaker circuitBreaker)
      Enables (or, with null, disables) the opt-in circuit breaker consulted for every request attempt. See CircuitBreaker for the open/half-open/closed semantics. Disabled by default.
      Parameters:
      circuitBreaker - the breaker to enforce, or null to disable

    • appendApiParams

      public void appendApiParams(String fileName) throws EquinixClientException
      Merges a domain's apiParams resource into the shared catalogue. Thread-safe: the merge is copy-on-write under apiParamsLock and published atomically through the volatile clientResourceFile field (read via the Lombok-generated getClientResourceFile()), so request threads reading the tree concurrently (Jackson's ObjectNode is not safe for concurrent read/write) always see either the old or the fully-merged catalogue.
      Parameters:
      fileName - the classpath resource name (e.g. json/apiParams_Fabric.json)
      Throws:
      EquinixClientException - if the resource is missing, malformed, or does not declare a functionalAreas object

    • getOAuthToken

      public OAuthToken getOAuthToken()
      Returns the currently published OAuth token, or null if the client has not authenticated yet.

      This is a lock-free volatile read returning the latest published instance. For an atomic validity-then-use decision under concurrency, prefer the internal single-flight path in setStandardHeaders(EquinixRequest) which captures a consistent snapshot under tokenLock.

      Returns:
      the current OAuthToken, may be null.

    • setOAuthToken

      public void setOAuthToken(OAuthToken oAuthToken)
      Publishes a (re)authenticated OAuth token for use by subsequent requests.

      Publication is serialized through tokenLock so that a token obtained by a single-flight refresh becomes visible atomically with respect to other threads inspecting validity. Once stored, the volatile field guarantees the new instance is visible to all threads.

      Parameters:
      oAuthToken - the freshly obtained token, may be null to clear.

    • setAuthenticator

      public void setAuthenticator(Runnable authenticator)
      Wires the callback used to mint and publish an OAuth token for lazy authentication and re-authentication on expiry. The facade client supplies this; the core client invokes it when a request needs a token and none valid is published.
      Parameters:
      authenticator - the token-acquisition callback (it must publish via setOAuthToken(OAuthToken))

    • authenticate

      public void authenticate()
      Forces (re)authentication via the wired authenticator, single-flight under tokenLock. This is the explicit authenticate() entry point. The authenticating guard means the token request it issues (which itself flows through setStandardHeaders(EquinixRequest)) does not recurse into another authentication. No-op when no authenticator is wired.
